findings.evidence: run_build_mods() runs b_proc = subprocess.run(b_cmd, ..., check=False) at 1007-1015 but never reads b_proc.returncode. Results are derived only from regex matches of PASS/FAIL lines in stdout (1019-1051). A build_check.py crash, or any non-zero exit that prints no 'FAIL build:' line, adds no FAIL and no ERROR to counts, so the RESULT line and the exit code at 1176 report success.
findings.suggested_investigation: Check scripts/build_check.py exit codes on failure paths (e.g. an exception before any per-mod line is printed). Then run compat_check.py with a build_check stub that exits 1 without printing FAIL lines and confirm the overall exit code is 0 today. Verify whether a non-zero returncode should add an ERROR result for each build mod.
findings.why_it_matters: The build leg of the gate can pass when the build tool itself failed. The exit code of the subprocess is the authoritative signal and is discarded.

findings.evidence: json_tmp_path is created by NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False) at 1068-1069, so the file always exists before run_tests.py starts. The check at 1089 'if Path(json_tmp_path).is_file():' is therefore always true. If run_tests.py crashes or exits before writing JSON, the file is empty; json.loads at 1091 raises and the broad 'except Exception: pass' at 1112-1113 swallows it. The 'else' branch at 1114-1116 that adds counts['ERROR'] for a non-zero returncode is unreachable.
findings.suggested_investigation: Reproduce by pointing run_tests.py at a stub that exits 2 without writing its --json file, then run compat_check.py --since HEAD with a test item in the plan and check the RESULT line and exit code. Confirm that the empty-file case reaches the except at 1112. Fix direction: treat a missing or unparseable JSON as ERROR for every requested id, and use the returncode in that decision.
findings.why_it_matters: A test runner that dies before reporting produces zero results and zero FAIL/ERROR counts, so the compat gate exits 0 with no tests run. This is a gate that can no longer fail on runner crash.

findings.evidence: Line 1094 reads 'st = r.get("status", "PASS")' so any runner result that lacks a status key is counted as PASS in counts[st] at 1095. Result entries are appended to all_results unchanged (1093), so the JSON output shows them as well.
findings.suggested_investigation: Check scripts/run_tests.py result-writing code to see whether every result always has a 'status' key. Also compare len(results) with len(test_suite_ids) after parsing. The default should be an error state, not PASS.
findings.why_it_matters: A fail-open default turns malformed or partial runner output into a PASS. Nothing else in the file cross-checks that the number of PASS results matches the number of requested ids.

findings.evidence: Counts are accumulated with counts[st] = counts.get(st, 0) + 1 for any status string (1095), but the exit decision at 1176 uses only fail_cnt (FAIL) and err_cnt (ERROR). Any other status value from the runner (for example TIMEOUT or CRASH, if run_tests.py emits them) is recorded but never causes exit 1.
findings.suggested_investigation: Enumerate every status value that scripts/run_tests.py can write to its JSON. If any value other than PASS, SKIP, FAIL or ERROR exists, make the exit decision reject it.
findings.why_it_matters: Non-PASS, non-SKIP outcomes that are not spelled FAIL or ERROR would be silently accepted by the gate.

findings.evidence: narrow_plan_to_gog_scoping keeps only items of kind 'build' and the cpp:k2addr_test test (341-346), drops every other test, suite, wine and static item, then runs 'plan.gaps.clear()' (358). It also appends the note 'GOG-only: Steam runtime unchanged' (359) without running any Steam check. It is invoked at 918-923 whenever K2Addr.h is the only non-test touched file and is_k2addr_gog_only_diff returns True.
findings.suggested_investigation: Check which plan items come from K2Addr.h dependents (Steam-variant tests, static raw-address and allowlist checks, wine smokes) using compat_graph.py. Confirm they are dropped by narrow_plan_to_gog_scoping. Then test a K2Addr.h change in a Steam-only constant that falls inside the makeGog..kGog line range and check whether the narrowed plan still runs the Steam tests.
findings.why_it_matters: A K2Addr.h change that the diff heuristic classifies as GOG-only silently removes Steam-facing and static checks and clears the GAP list that --strict uses at 953 and 1180. The printed claim that Steam is unchanged is not verified by this code.

findings.evidence: The docstring (230) says the check verifies that hunks 'touch only the kGog initializer'. The code (256-259) only verifies that each hunk's old and new line ranges fall inside the span from the 'makeGog()' constexpr line to the first 'kGog =' line (209-222). Any edit to other lines in that span, such as a change to the makeGog() body or another constant between those lines, passes and triggers the GOG-only narrowing.
findings.suggested_investigation: Read K2Addr.h around the makeGog() block to see what lines fall between 'makeGog()' and 'kGog ='. Make a test edit to a line in that span that is not the kGog initializer and check whether is_k2addr_gog_only_diff returns True. Tighten the check to compare the changed line text against the kGog initializer pattern.
findings.why_it_matters: The narrowing is a safety reduction. Its precondition is weaker than its documentation, so non-GOG-specific edits can reduce test coverage.

findings.evidence: When a smoke has no 'mod' key and mods_by_stem has no match, the fallback loops over (repo_root / 'patch_manager_mods').iterdir() without sorting and takes the first directory where 'clean in stem or stem in clean' (423). The chosen directory decides candidate_sources (436-439). If the wrong directory is chosen, or a directory with old mtimes is chosen, the newest-source comparison at 444-448 can report a stale kpatch as fresh and skip the STALE marking.
findings.suggested_investigation: List the smokes in perf_lab_src/harness/smokes.toml that lack a 'mod' key and check which directory the fallback selects for each. Check whether any of them has a short clean name that matches the wrong mod. Make the directory iteration order deterministic and prefer an exact match.
findings.why_it_matters: The stale-kpatch check that protects smoke results from older DLLs depends on a substring match that is not deterministic and can select an unrelated mod.

findings.evidence: Stale wine smokes are recorded as status 'SKIP' with reason 'unverified (stale kpatch)' (981-989). The exit logic returns 1 only for FAIL or ERROR (1176-1177) and returns 3 for SKIP only when --strict is given (1180-1181). Without --strict, a run whose only unverified items are stale smokes exits 0.
findings.suggested_investigation: Run compat_check.py --wine on a case where a smoke's kpatch is older than its source, without --strict, and confirm the exit code is 0. Check the policy text that tells agents whether skipped or unverified items block a downstream step.
findings.why_it_matters: The repository rule that a rebuilt .kpatch needs a fresh gate PASS before install is not enforced by the default exit code. A stale kpatch is reported as a warning only.

findings.evidence: Lint parses each test.toml inside 'try: ... except Exception: pass' (601-623), so a malformed test.toml drops its covers silently. run_lint always returns 0 (715), and main returns 3 only with --strict (850-851).
findings.suggested_investigation: Add a malformed test.toml fixture and run --lint to see whether any warning is produced. Check whether lint is referenced as a required gate in the policy docs. If so, the exit code should reflect warnings.
findings.why_it_matters: Broad exception handling can hide malformed test manifests from --lint. Without --strict, lint warnings never fail the command.

notes: Analysis is from the packet content only; no tool calls were made. Not verified: scripts/build_check.py and scripts/run_tests.py output and exit-code behaviour, and compat_graph.py (plan contents, and whether graph.kpm_dir can be None, which would make check_stale_wine_smokes raise at line 978 when --wine is set). Install or live-game reachability through --kpm-dir (passed to build_check at 1002-1003) could not be assessed without reading build_check.py. No secrets or credential paths were touched.
